records.name: Philadelphia Medical Reserve Corps
records.summary: A city volunteer unit that helps during public health emergencies, disasters, and big public events such as the marathon. You do not need a medical background to join.
records.what_you_do: Register online, pass a background check, attend an orientation, then take trainings and get called for deployments when needed. Medical volunteers give screenings, medicines, or vaccines; others answer phones, do data entry, or interpret.

schedule.text: Deployments are called as needed. The city asks each volunteer to do at least one training, exercise, or deployment a year.

first_step.how: Register online through the state volunteer sign-up site (linked from the city page), pass the background check, then attend an in-person or virtual orientation
first_step.basis: Anyone 18 or older can apply online and the city publishes the steps, though a background check comes first

records.notes: Dated evidence is thin: the page is current but its newest dated item is a 2024 volunteer manual, so status is probably_active. Member count is given as more than 5,000 on one city page and more than 7,000 on another, so the count is left out. Volunteers may be deployed outside the city too.

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Search and Rescue (GPSAR)
records.summary: A volunteer group that searches for missing people across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Delaware. Its searches are free for families, and its volunteers train in search skills and stay on call around the clock.
records.what_you_do: Search teams, land navigation, logistics, search planning, and communications. Members train in search skills and help run searches once they are dispatched.

schedule.text: On call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for dispatch. No regular meeting schedule is published.

cost.text: Searches are free to the public. No volunteer fee is listed.

first_step.how: Answer the application questions on the volunteer page, then call or email the membership chair
first_step.basis: Needs an application and a conversation with the membership chair before you see what the work is like; the page calls it a substantial commitment

records.notes: Based in Glenside, outside the city, but recruits and serves across the region including Philadelphia, so in_city is false. The site says founded 1977. The volunteer page lists 877-598-5618 and chief@gpsar.org while the main site lists 877-255-5678 and gpsar@gpsar.org; both are recorded as published. No dated organization news found, so status is probably_active from the working site. Minimum age is not stated.

records.name: Temple University EMS (TUEMS)
records.summary: A student-run volunteer ambulance crew at Temple that gives basic life support care on campus and in the nearby North Philadelphia neighborhood. Its clinical members are certified EMTs.
records.what_you_do: Provide basic medical care at emergencies on and near Temple's main campus, working with Temple police and the Philadelphia Fire Department.

schedule.text: Shifts and meeting times are not published on the group's page.

first_step.how: Open the Join TUEMS page on the group's site or email tuems@temple.edu
first_step.basis: A join page exists, but the steps, training, and age rules are not described

records.notes: The page does not say membership is limited to students, but the group is student-run and the audience was set to students for that reason. The News section shows no dated items, so status is probably_active. Verify the audience before relying on it.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Second Alarmers Association
leads_only.note: All-volunteer group that brings food, rest and supplies to police and firefighters at emergencies, based at a station in East Falls. Listed by the city's volunteer page. Found news from 2019 and 2021 confirming it, but no website or join details. Only a Facebook page was found, so not checked further.
